body: Enron peaked at ~$90 in Aug 2000 (market cap ~$70 bn) and filed for bankruptcy on 2 Dec 2001 with the stock under $1. Mechanics: mark-to-market accounting booked the estimated lifetime profit of long-dated energy contracts upfront; off-balance-sheet special-purpose entities (Chewco, LJM, Raptors) run by CFO Andrew Fastow hid debt and hedged Enron's own stock; restatement of 1997-2001 earnings in Nov 2001; auditor Arthur Andersen shredded documents and collapsed. Visible flags: (1) reported earnings far above operating cash flow (much 'cash flow' came from asset sales and prepay deals); (2) low return on capital (~single digit) despite 'asset-light' trading claims; (3) opaque segment disclosure -- Bethany McLean's Fortune article 'Is Enron Overpriced?' (5 Mar 2001) asked simply how Enron made money; (4) Jim Chanos (Kynikos) shorted from late 2000 on poor ROIC vs cost of capital, related-party SPEs and insider selling; (5) executives sold large blocks of stock in 2000-01; (6) CEO Skilling resigned abruptly in Aug 2001 after six months; (7) Cornell MBA students flagged Enron with the Beneish M-score in 1998. Lesson: when you can't explain how a company earns cash, assume it doesn't; related-party entities run by the CFO and CEO departures 'for personal reasons' are disqualifiers.

data.early_signals: earnings >> CFO; low ROIC; SPEs run by CFO; insider selling; abrupt CEO exit; M-score flag 1998

body: FTX was valued at ~$32 bn in early 2022 with backers including Sequoia, SoftBank and Temasek. On 2 Nov 2022 CoinDesk (Ian Allison) published sister firm Alameda Research's balance sheet: a large share of its ~$14.6 bn assets was FTT, the token FTX itself issued ($3.66 bn 'unlocked FTT' + $2.16 bn 'FTT collateral'). Binance said on 6 Nov it would sell its FTT; withdrawals surged; FTX halted withdrawals on 8 Nov and filed for bankruptcy on 11 Nov. Customer deposits had been lent to Alameda (shortfall widely reported ~$8 bn). Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted in Nov 2023 and sentenced to 25 years in Mar 2024. (Bankruptcy estate later recovered enough to repay customers in full on petition-date values due to asset recoveries and crypto prices -- not a vindication.) Visible flags: (1) no independent board, no CFO, no risk committee; (2) a related proprietary trading firm owned by the exchange founder; (3) self-issued token used as collateral = circular value; (4) obscure auditors for a $30 bn firm; (5) offshore domicile (Bahamas) and opaque related-party loans to executives; (6) VCs admitted minimal diligence. Lesson: circular collateral and related-party trading arms are the purest disqualifiers; custody of your assets with an unregulated counterparty is credit risk.

data.early_signals: no board/CFO; Alameda related party; FTT collateral; small auditors; offshore
